{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01S36kMzRTgu8SujRpPrpBPh","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# SDS\n     2→\n     3→SDS (Self-Defining Systems) is an AI-native approach that embeds agentic LLMs into the full systems lifecycle—specification, design, implementation, and operation—to autonomously explore, validate, and evolve infrastructure.\n     4→\n     5→## Overview\n     6→\n     7→This repository contains applications, tools, and infrastructure code for the SDS project.\n     8→\n     9→## Project Structure\n    10→\n    11→```\n    12→sds/\n    13→├── app_operator/    # Application operators and management tools\n    14→│   ├── agents/      # Specialized agents (deployer, monitor)\n    15→│   └── ...\n    16→├── apps/            # Application code and configurations\n    17→├── scripts/         # Helper scripts (formatting, checks)\n    18→├── sds_operator     # CLI tool for running the operator\n    19→├── tests/           # Unit tests\n    20→└── tools/           # Shared tools/utilities\n    21→```\n    22→\n    23→## Application Operator\n    24→\n    25→The Application Operator (`app_operator`) is a tool for deploying and monitoring applications with automated health checks and graceful lifecycle management. It also includes AI-powered script generation to automatically create deployment and health check scripts for any application repository.\n    26→\n    27→### Key Features\n    28→\n    29→- **AI-Powered Script Generation**: Automatically generate deployment and health check scripts for any repository using LLM analysis\n    30→- **Automated Deployment**: Deploy applications with a single command\n    31→- **Continuous Health Monitoring**: Periodic health checks with intelligent summaries\n    32→- **Graceful Lifecycle Management**: Clean startup and shutdown handling\n    33→- **LLM-Powered Insights**: Health check summaries generated using OpenAI models\n    34→\n    35→### Quick Start\n    36→\n    37→#### Installation\n    38→\n    39→From the project root:\n    40→\n    41→```bash\n    42→uv sync\n    43→```\n    44→\n    45→Or using pip:\n    46→\n    47→```bash\n    48→pip install -e .\n    49→```\n    50→\n    51→#### Environment Setup\n    52→\n    53→1. Create a `.env` file in the project root with the necessary API keys and configuration.\n    54→\n    55→For OpenAI (required for Codex agent):\n    56→```bash\n    57→OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here\n    58→```\n    59→\n    60→For Gemini Agent (Vertex AI):\n    61→```bash\n    62→GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=\"path/to/your/credentials.json\"\n    63→GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=\"your_project_id\"\n    64→GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=\"global\"\n    65→```\n    66→\n    67→2. Configure the agent and operator settings by copying `sds.example.toml` to `sds.toml` in the project root:\n    68→\n    69→```bash\n    70→cp sds.example.toml sds.toml\n    71→```\n    72→\n    73→Then edit `sds.toml` to configure your settings:\n    74→\n    75→```toml\n    76→[agent]\n    77→provider = \"codex\"  # or \"gemini\", \"claude\"\n    78→model = \"gpt-4o-mini\" # optional\n    79→\n    80→[operator]\n    81→interval = 30 # Health check interval in seconds (default: 30)\n    82→monitoring_max_iters = 5 # Maximum number of health monitoring iterations (default: 5)\n    83→deployment_max_iters = 5 # Maximum deployment attempts (default: 5)\n    84→\n    85→[deployment]\n    86→platform = \"docker\" # Deployment platform: \"docker\" or \"k8s\" (default: \"docker\")\n    87→target = \"local\"    # Deployment target: \"local\" or \"remote\" (default: \"local\")\n    88→```\n    89→\n    90→### Experiment Workflow\n    91→\n    92→#### 1. Create an Experiment\n    93→\n    94→First, create an isolated experiment environment from an existing application using `init-exp`.\n    95→\n    96→```bash\n    97→./sds_operator init-exp apps/target-app my-experiment-name\n    98→```\n    99→This copies the application to `exp/<app-name>/<exp-name>`, removes existing git history and SDS configurations, and initializes a new git repository.\n   100→\n   101→#### 2. Run the Experiment\n   102→\n   103→Next, use the `run` command to deploy and monitor the experiment using an AI agent.\n   104→\n   105→```bash\n   106→./sds_operator run exp/target-app/my-experiment-name\n   107→```\n   108→\n   109→**What it does:**\n   110→- **Auto-Scripting**: Automatically generates deployment and health check scripts if they are missing. Scripts are created in `<app-dir>/.sds`.\n   111→- **Self-Healing Deployment**: If a deployment fails, the AI agent analyzes the error logs, identifies the root cause, and automatically fixes the scripts before retrying (up to 5 attempts).\n   112→- **AI-Powered Analysis**: Provides intelligent analysis of health check results to suggest improvements.\n   113→\n   114→### Command Reference\n   115→\n   116→#### `run` - Deploy and Monitor\n   117→\n   118→Deploy an application with autonomous error fixing and AI-powered health monitoring.\n   119→\n   120→**Usage:**\n   121→```bash\n   122→./sds_operator run <DIR> [options]\n   123→```\n   124→\n   125→**Arguments:**\n   126→- `DIR`: Path to the repository directory (required, positional argument)\n   127→\n   128→**Options:**\n   129→- `--config <FILE>`: Path to configuration file (default: `sds.toml` in target dir)\n   130→\n   131→#### `init-exp` - Initialize Experiment\n   132→\n   133→Initialize a new experiment from an existing application.\n   134→\n   135→**Usage:**\n   136→```bash\n   137→./sds_operator init-exp <APP_PATH> <EXP_NAME>\n   138→```\n   139→\n   140→**Arguments:**\n   141→- `APP_PATH`: Path to the source application directory\n   142→- `EXP_NAME`: Name of the new experiment\n   143→\n   144→### AI-Assisted Contribution Workflow\n   145→\n   146→SDS supports AI-assisted contributions using coding agent skills (currently available in Claude, Gemini, and Opencode agents).\n   147→\n   148→**Workflow:**\n   149→\n   150→1. **Create a branch**: Use the `git-branch` skill to create a new feature branch\n   151→2. **Make commits**: Use the `git-commit` skill to create commits with AI-generated messages\n   152→3. **Prepare PR**: Use the `pr-prepare` skill to generate a comprehensive PR description\n   153→4. **Open PR**: Create a merge request on GitLab with the generated content\n   154→\n   155→**Example:**\n   156→\n   157→```bash\n   158→# In Claude (use \"/\" prefix):\n   159→/git-branch \"add monitoring alerts\"\n   160→# ... edit files ...\n   161→/git-commit\n   162→/pr-prepare  # Automatically pushes branch to remote\n   163→\n   164→# In opencode or gemini-cli (no \"/\" prefix needed):\n   165→git-branch \"add monitoring alerts\"\n   166→# ... edit files ...\n   167→git-commit\n   168→pr-prepare  # Automatically pushes branch to remote\n   169→\n   170→# Then create MR on GitLab using the generated title and description\n   171→```\n   172→\n   173→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BLt1uJikgrCR7ejhyfS6q3","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# SDS (Self-Defining Systems)\n     2→\n     3→**Context for LLM Agent**\n     4→\n     5→SDS is an AI-native project designed to autonomously explore, validate, and evolve infrastructure by embedding agentic LLMs into the system lifecycle. It primarily consists of an **Application Operator** (an intelligent agent) and the **DeathStarBench** suite (microservices benchmarks) used as target applications.\n     6→\n     7→## Project Structure\n     8→\n     9→```\n    10→sds/\n    11→├── app_operator/    # Core operator logic.\n    12→│   ├── agents/      # Specialized agents (deployer, monitor).\n    13→│   └── ...\n    14→├── apps/            # Application code (DeathStarBench suite).\n    15→│   └── deathstarbench/\n    16→│       ├── hotelReservation/ # Go-based microservices app.\n    17→│       ├── socialNetwork/    # C++/Python/Go microservices app.\n    18→│       └── ...\n    19→├── tools/           # Shared tools/utilities (e.g., healthcheck).\n    20→└── README.md        # Root project documentation.\n    21→```\n    22→\n    23→## 1. Application Operator (`app_operator/`)\n    24→\n    25→The **Application Operator** is a Python tool that autonomously deploys, monitors, and manages applications. It uses AI agents (Codex, Gemini, or Claude) to self-correct deployment scripts and summarize health checks.\n    26→\n    27→### Setup & Usage\n    28→\n    29→*   **Dependency Management:** Uses `uv` (or `pip`).\n    30→*   **Installation:**\n    31→    ```bash\n    32→    uv sync  # or pip install -e .\n    33→    ```\n    34→*   **Environment:** Requires `.env` in root with `OPENAI_API_KEY`.\n    35→\n    36→### Key Commands\n    37→\n    38→*   **Default Mode (AI-assisted Autonomous Deployment):**\n    39→    This mode attempts to deploy the application in the specified repository, using an AI agent to automatically fix deployment errors.\n    40→    ```bash\n    41→    # Uses Codex, Gemini, or Claude as configured in sds.toml\n    42→    ./sds_operator /path/to/repo\n    43→    ```\n    44→\n    45→### Coding Agent Configuration\n    46→\n    47→You can specify which AI provider to use for script generation and fixing by adding an `sds.toml` file to the target repository:\n    48→\n    49→```toml\n    50→[agent]\n    51→provider = \"gemini\"  # Valid: \"gemini\", \"codex\", \"claude\", \"claude-code\", \"opencode\"\n    52→model = \"gemini-1.5-pro\" # optional\n    53→\n    54→[operator]\n    55→interval = 30 # Health check interval in seconds (1-86400, default: 30)\n    56→monitoring_max_iters = 5 # Maximum health monitoring iterations (>0, default: 5)\n    57→deployment_max_iters = 5 # Maximum deployment attempts (>0, default: 5)\n    58→```\n    59→\n    60→**Note**: Invalid configuration values will raise `ValueError` or `TypeError` with clear error messages at initialization.\n    61→\n    62→### Architecture\n    63→The operator uses specialized agents to manage the application lifecycle:\n    64→\n    65→*   **DeploymentAgent (`app_operator/agents/deployer.py`):**\n    66→    *   Generates deployment scripts (`deploy.sh`, `health_check.sh`) if missing.\n    67→    *   Deploys the application and automatically fixes errors using an AI agent.\n    68→    *   Manages the self-healing deployment loop.\n    69→*   **CodeAnalyzerAgent (`app_operator/agents/code_analyzer.py`):**\n    70→    *   Analyzes the codebase before deployment.\n    71→    *   Generates `.sds/code_analysis.md` and `.sds/deployment_issues.md`.\n    72→    *   Identifies potential deployment issues proactively.\n    73→*   **AppMonitor (`app_operator/agents/app_monitor.py`):**\n    74→    *   Monitors application health at regular intervals.\n    75→    *   Uses `HealthCheckTask` to execute checks and `CodingAgent` to analyze results.\n    76→*   **Configuration (`app_operator/config.py`):**\n    77→    *   `AgentConfig`: AI provider configuration (codex, gemini, claude, claude-code, opencode)\n    78→    *   `OperatorConfig`: Operational parameters (intervals, max iterations)\n    79→    *   All configs validate on initialization with clear error messages\n    80→*   **Exceptions (`app_operator/exceptions.py`):**\n    81→    *   Custom exception hierarchy for clear error categorization\n    82→    *   Exceptions include context (exit codes, attempt numbers, timeout flags)\n    83→*   **Filesystem (`app_operator/filesystem.py`):**\n    84→    *   Abstraction layer for filesystem operations\n    85→    *   `RealFilesystem`: Production implementation\n    86→    *   `InMemoryFilesystem`: Testing implementation (fast, isolated)\n    87→*   **Tools (`tools/`):**\n    88→    *   `healthcheck.py`: Encapsulates health check execution logic.\n    89→\n    90→## 2. Applications (`apps/deathstarbench/`)\n    91→\n    92→**DeathStarBench** is a suite of cloud microservices benchmarks.\n    93→\n    94→*   **Hotel Reservation:** A Go-based microservice application for booking hotels.\n    95→    *   **Tech Stack:** Go, gRPC, Consul, MongoDB, Memcached, Jaeger.\n    96→    *   **Ports:** Frontend at `http://localhost:5000`.\n    97→*   **Social Network:** A mixed-language social graph application.\n    98→*   **Media Microservices:** Service for streaming/processing media.\n    99→\n   100→## Development Conventions\n   101→\n   102→*   **Python (Agents):**\n   103→    *   Uses type hints.\n   104→    *   Uses `autopep8` for formatting.\n   105→    *   Uses `ruff` for static analysis.\n   106→    *   Tests via `pytest`.\n   107→    *   Dataclasses use `__post_init__` for validation (see `app_operator/config.py`).\n   108→    *   Custom exception hierarchy in `app_operator/exceptions.py` for clear error handling.\n   109→*   **Microservices:**\n   110→    *   Standard `docker-compose` patterns.\n   111→    *   Go modules for Go services.\n   112→    *   Service discovery via Consul is a common pattern.\n   113→\n   114→## Usage Guide for LLM agents\n   115→\n   116→*   **When debugging deployment:** Check `.sds/deploy.sh` and the generated logs.\n   117→*   **When adding a new app:** Simply run the operator on the repository. The `DeploymentAgent` will attempt to generate appropriate scripts automatically.\n   118→*   **When adding a new feature:** Think of what new behavior(s) are being introduced, and how you would test them. Test public behavior, not internal implementation details.\n   119→*   **When fixing bugs:** Think of how to write test(s) to reproduce the issue first and then use them to verify your fix. The test should be part of your fix. If you cannot do so, you must defend your decision.\n   120→\n   121→## Notes from the developers\n   122→\n   123→*   Keep this file up to date when you update the project.\n   124→*   Use `uv` and `uv run ...` for running python.\n   125→*   When code update impacts the CLI interface, update the README.\n   126→*   Remember to format the code after code edits using `@scripts/format_code.sh`.\n   127→\n   128→### Documentation\n   129→\n   130→*   Update README.md when your changes impact the user-facing behavior.\n   131→\n   132→### Code hygiene\n   133→\n   134→* When removing code, do not comment it out, just remove it.\n   135→\n   136→### Code Validation\n   137→\n   138→*   **Formatting:** Run `@scripts/format_code.sh` on python code edits.\n   139→*   **Linting:** Run `@scripts/check_errors.sh` on python code edits. Add `--fix` to automatically fix errors.\n   140→\n   141→### Testing\n   142→\n   143→#### Test Organization\n   144→\n   145→*   **Unit tests** (`tests/unit/`): Fast, isolated tests for individual components\n   146→*   **Integration tests** (`tests/integration/`): Test component interactions and real behavior\n   147→*   Test organization by component:\n   148→    *   `tests/unit/config/`: Configuration validation tests\n   149→    *   `tests/unit/agents/`: Agent-specific tests (deployment, monitoring)\n   150→    *   `tests/integration/`: End-to-end scenarios, signal handling, concurrency\n   151→\n   152→#### Running Tests\n   153→\n   154→*   Run all tests: `uv run pytest tests/`\n   155→*   Run specific category: `uv run pytest tests/unit/` or `uv run pytest tests/integration/`\n   156→*   Run with coverage: `uv run pytest tests/ --cov=app_operator`\n   157→*   Check if tests pass after you've modified the codebase's behavior.\n   158→*   Don't run the sds_operator directly to test; it is a long-running process that will not terminate.\n   159→\n   160→#### Writing Tests - Best Practices\n   161→\n   162→**1. Test Behavior, Not Implementation**\n   163→```python\n   164→# ✅ GOOD: Test observable outcomes\n   165→def test_deployment_succeeds_after_retry(repo_with_scripts):\n   166→    operator = AppOperator(str(repo), agent=agent, max_deployment_attempts=3)\n   167→    exit_code = operator.run()\n   168→    assert exit_code == 0\n   169→    assert (repo / \".sds\" / \"logs\" / \"deploy_attempt_2.log\").exists()\n   170→\n   171→# ❌ AVOID: Test internal method calls (brittle)\n   172→def test_deployment():\n   173→    mock_deployer._fix_with_agent.assert_called_once()  # Fragile!\n   174→```\n   175→\n   176→**2. Use Test Fixtures**\n   177→\n   178→Available fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`:\n   179→*   `test_filesystem`: In-memory filesystem for fast, isolated tests\n   180→*   `stub_agent`: Minimal agent that returns simple responses\n   181→*   `error_agent`: Agent that always raises errors\n   182→*   `timeout_agent`: Agent that simulates timeouts\n   183→*   `tracking_agent`: Agent that tracks all calls for verification\n   184→*   `configurable_agent`: Agent with configurable responses\n   185→*   `repo_with_scripts`: Temp repository with pre-generated working scripts\n   186→\n   187→**3. Test Agent Doubles**\n   188→\n   189→Use test doubles from `tests/fixtures/agents.py` instead of mocking:\n   190→```python\n   191→from tests.fixtures.agents import StubAgent, TrackingAgent, ErrorAgent\n   192→\n   193→def test_deployment_with_agent(tmp_path):\n   194→    agent = StubAgent()  # Simple, predictable behavior\n   195→    deployer = DeploymentAgent(tmp_path, agent)\n   196→    result = deployer.run(max_attempts=1)\n   197→    assert result is True\n   198→\n   199→def test_agent_interaction(tmp_path):\n   200→    agent = TrackingAgent()  # Tracks calls for verification\n   201→    deployer = DeploymentAgent(tmp_path, agent)\n   202→    deployer.run(max_attempts=2)\n   203→    assert agent.generation_count == 1\n   204→```\n   205→\n   206→**4. Filesystem Abstraction**\n   207→\n   208→For testing filesystem operations without disk I/O:\n   209→```python\n   210→from app_operator.filesystem import InMemoryFilesystem\n   211→\n   212→def test_with_memory_filesystem():\n   213→    fs = InMemoryFilesystem()\n   214→    fs.simulate_permission_error(path)  # Test error handling\n   215→    # ... test code that uses filesystem\n   216→```\n   217→\n   218→**5. Configuration Validation**\n   219→\n   220→All configuration dataclasses validate in `__post_init__`:\n   221→*   `AgentConfig`: Validates provider (must be in VALID_PROVIDERS), model type\n   222→*   `OperatorConfig`: Validates interval (1-86400s), max_iters (positive integers)\n   223→*   Invalid configs raise `TypeError` or `ValueError` with clear messages\n   224→\n   225→When adding new config fields:\n   226→```python\n   227→@dataclass\n   228→class MyConfig:\n   229→    field: int = 10\n   230→\n   231→    def __post_init__(self):\n   232→        if not isinstance(self.field, int):\n   233→            raise TypeError(f\"field must be int, got {type(self.field).__name__}\")\n   234→        if self.field <= 0:\n   235→            raise ValueError(f\"field must be positive, got {self.field}\")\n   236→```\n   237→\n   238→**6. Exception Handling**\n   239→\n   240→Use custom exceptions from `app_operator/exceptions.py`:\n   241→*   `ConfigurationError`: Configuration issues\n   242→*   `DeploymentError`: Deployment failures (includes exit_code, attempt)\n   243→*   `FileSystemError`: Filesystem operation failures\n   244→*   `ProcessError`: Process execution errors (includes timeout flag)\n   245→*   `AgentError`: Agent-related failures\n   246→\n   247→Example:\n   248→```python\n   249→from app_operator.exceptions import DeploymentError\n   250→\n   251→if result.exit_code != 0:\n   252→    raise DeploymentError(\n   253→        \"Deployment failed\",\n   254→        exit_code=result.exit_code,\n   255→        attempt=current_attempt\n   256→    )\n   257→```\n   258→\n   259→#### Test Coverage Guidelines\n   260→\n   261→When introducing new features or modifying existing behavior:\n   262→*   Write tests for the **happy path** (expected behavior)\n   263→*   Write tests for **error conditions** (permission denied, timeouts, invalid input)\n   264→*   Write tests for **boundary values** (0, 1, max values)\n   265→*   Write tests for **edge cases** (special characters, long paths, concurrent operations)\n   266→*   Update tests on application semantic changes\n   267→\n   268→#### What NOT to Test\n   269→\n   270→*   Don't test private implementation details (methods starting with `_`)\n   271→*   Don't test third-party library behavior\n   272→*   Don't write tests that duplicate other tests\n   273→*   Don't test obvious getters/setters without logic\n   274→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. Environment variables (API keys)\n```\n\n---\n\n### **3. Key Components & Modules**\n\n#### **A. Core Operator (app_operator/operator.py)**\n- **Main orchestrator** for the deployment & monitoring workflow\n- Manages the 3-phase lifecycle:\n  1. **Code Analysis** - Pre-deployment codebase analysis\n  2. **Deployment** - Deploy with automatic AI-assisted error recovery\n  3. **Monitoring** - Continuous health checks with intelligent analysis\n- Handles graceful shutdown via signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM)\n- Manages trajectory recording for execution traces\n\n#### **B. AI Coding Agents (agent_cli/)**\nAbstraction layer for multiple LLM providers with a unified interface:\n\n| Agent | Provider | Use Case |\n|-------|----------|----------|\n| **CodexCodingAgent** | OpenAI Codex CLI | Code generation via OpenAI |\n| **GeminiCodingAgent** | Google Gemini CLI | Generation via Google Gemini with event streaming |\n| **ClaudeCodeCodingAgent** | Claude Code CLI | AI-native generation via Anthropic's Claude |\n| **OpencodeCodingAgent** | OpenCode CLI | Code generation via OpenCode |\n\n- All agents inherit from abstract `CodingAgent` base class\n- `CLICodingAgent` provides CLI-based execution foundation\n- Factory pattern (`factory.py`) selects agents via `sds.toml` configuration\n- Agents handle timeouts, signal interruption, and stream processing\n\n#### **C. Specialized Agents**\n\n**1. DeploymentAgent** (agents/deployer.py)\n- Auto-generates `deploy.sh` and `health_check.sh` if missing\n- Executes deployment with timeout handling\n- Implements self-healing loop: deployment → failure detection → AI fix → retry\n- Supports multiple deployment platforms (Docker, Kubernetes)\n- Tracks attempt history and logs\n\n**2. CodeAnalyzerAgent** (agents/code_analyzer.py)\n- Analyzes codebase structure before deployment\n- Generates `.sds/code_analysis.md` (findings)\n- Generates `.sds/deployment_issues.md` (identified problems)\n- Uses agent to explore repo and identify deployment challenges\n\n**3. AppMonitor** (agents/app_monitor.py)\n- Runs periodic health checks at configurable intervals\n- Executes extensible monitoring tasks via `MonitoringTask` interface\n- `HealthCheckTask` - Runs `.sds/health_check.sh` and analyzes results\n- Uses agent to interpret health check output and suggest improvements\n- Tracks health check cycle count\n\n#### **D. Configuration System (config.py)**\nDataclass-based configuration with strict validation:\n\n```python\nAgentConfig       # provider, model selection\nOperatorConfig    # interval (1-86400s), deployment_max_iters, monitoring_max_iters\nDeploymentConfig  # platform (docker/k8s), target (local/remote)\n```\n\n- Configuration hierarchy: project root → target repo → `.sds/config.toml`\n- Supports TOML format via `tomllib`/`tomli`\n- Validates on initialization with clear error messages\n- Merges configurations with deep merge for overrides\n\n#### **E. Filesystem Abstraction (filesystem.py)**\n- Interface-based design for testability\n- `RealFilesystem` - Production file operations\n- `InMemoryFilesystem` - Testing without disk I/O\n- Abstracts: exists, is_dir, mkdir, read_text, write_text, chmod\n- Enables dependency injection for better unit testing\n\n#### **F. Exception Hierarchy (exceptions.py)**\nCustom exceptions with context:\n- `SdsOperatorError` - Base exception\n- `ConfigurationError` - Config validation failures\n- `DeploymentError` - Includes exit_code, attempt number\n- `FileSystemError` - File operation failures\n- `ProcessError` - Subprocess failures with timeout flag\n- `AgentError` - Agent generation/analysis failures\n\n#### **G. Trajectory Recording (tools/trajectory.py)**\nReal-time execution trace capture:\n- Records all agent interactions, prompts, responses, tool calls\n- Four phases: EXPLORATION, SCRIPT_GENERATION, DEPLOYMENT, MONITORING\n- Thread-safe singleton pattern\n- Outputs to `.sds/trajectory.json`\n- Limits output to prevent huge files (MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=10000 chars)\n- Supports Gemini session cleanup\n\n#### **H. Health Check System (tools/healthcheck.py)**\n- Executes `.sds/health_check.sh` with timeout\n- Captures stdout/stderr/exit_code\n- Writes logs to `.sds/logs/health_check_*.log`\n- Handles timeouts gracefully with partial output capture\n- Returns structured result dict\n\n---\n\n### **4. Programming Languages & Technologies**\n\n| Language | Usage | Key Files |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **Python 3.10+** | Core operator, agents, tools | app_operator/*, tools/* |\n| **Bash** | Deployment/health check scripts (auto-generated) | `.sds/deploy.sh`, `.sds/health_check.sh` |\n| **Go** | Target applications (Hotel Reservation) | apps/deathstarbench/hotelReservation/* |\n| **Java** | Target applications (Train Ticket) | apps/train-ticket/* |\n| **C++/Python** | Mixed-language microservices | apps/deathstarbench/socialNetwork/* |\n| **Jinja2** | Prompt templating | prompts/*.jinja2 |\n| **TOML** | Configuration files | sds.toml, config.toml |\n\n**Key Dependencies:**\n- `langchain-openai>=1.1.6` - LLM integration\n- `langgraph>=1.0.5` - Agentic workflows\n- `python-dotenv` - Environment variable loading\n- `loguru` - Structured logging\n- `jinja2` - Template rendering\n- `pytest` - Testing framework\n\n---\n\n### **5. CLI Commands & Entry Points**\n\n**Entry Point:** `sds_operator` (bash wrapper)\n```bash\n./sds_operator run <DIR> [--config <FILE>]      # Deploy & monitor\n./sds_operator init-exp <APP_PATH> <EXP_NAME>   # Create experiment\n```\n\n**Commands Implementation:**\n- `commands/run.py` - Orchestrates AppOperator with loaded config\n- `commands/init_exp.py` - Copies app, removes git history, initializes fresh repo\n\n**Dependencies Check:**\n- Validates Docker and kubectl are installed\n- Checks Docker daemon is running\n\n---\n\n### **6. Configuration Flow**\n\n```\nsds.toml (root) or target/.sds/config.toml\n    ↓\nAgentConfig (provider selection)\n    ↓\nCreate agent via factory\n    ↓\nAppOperator initialization\n    ↓\nLoad or override via runtime flags\n```\n\n**Configuration Priority:**\n1. Project root `sds.toml`\n2. Target repo `sds.toml`\n3. Target repo `.sds/config.toml`\n4. CLI flags override\n\n---\n\n### **7. Deployment Workflow**\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                 AppOperator.run()                   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                        │\n        ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐\n        ▼               ▼               ▼\n   [Analysis]      [Deployment]     [Monitoring]\n        │               │               │\n        │       ┌──────────────────┐    │\n        │       │ Check/Generate   │    │\n        │       │ deploy.sh &      │    │\n        │       │ health_check.sh  │    │\n        │       └──────────────────┘    │\n        │               │               │\n        │       ┌──────────────────┐    │\n        │       │ Run deploy.sh    │    │\n        │       └──────────────────┘    │\n        │               │               │\n        │           Failed? ──── Use AI ├─ Analyze & Fix\n        │               │               │\n        │       ┌──────────────────┐    │\n        │       │ Retry if max     │    │\n        │       │ attempts < N     │    │\n        │       └──────────────────┘    │\n        │               │               │\n        └───────────────┼───────────────┘\n                        │\n                 Success ✓\n```\n\n---\n\n### **8. Test Structure**\n\n**Unit Tests** (`tests/unit/`)\n- `test_config.py` - Configuration validation\n- `test_deployment_agent.py` - Deployment logic\n- `test_app_monitor.py` - Monitoring tasks\n- `test_deployer_script_generation.py` - Script auto-generation\n- Agent-specific tests for Gemini, Claude, Codex\n\n**Integration Tests** (`tests/integration/`)\n- `test_integration.py` - End-to-end workflows\n- `test_signal_handling.py` - Graceful shutdown\n- `test_init_exp.py` - Experiment initialization\n- `test_trajectory_integration.py` - Trajectory recording\n\n**Fixtures** (`tests/fixtures/`)\n- `agents.py` - Test double agents (StubAgent, TrackingAgent, ErrorAgent)\n- `filesystems.py` - In-memory filesystem for testing\n\n---\n\n### **9. Target Applications**\n\n**DeathStarBench Suite** - Microservices benchmarks\n- **Hotel Reservation** - Go gRPC microservices (Consul, MongoDB, Memcached, Jaeger)\n- **Social Network** - Mixed-language social graph application\n- **Media Microservices** - Media streaming/processing\n\n**Train Ticket** - Large distributed Java microservices system with 50+ services\n\n---\n\n### **10. Claude AI Integration**\n\nThe project includes Claude AI Code integration via skills (`.claude/skills/`):\n- **git-branch** - Create feature branches with naming convention\n- **git-commit** - Generate conventional commit messages\n- **pr-prepare** - Auto-generate PR descriptions from diffs\n- **skill-creator** - Framework for creating new skills\n\nThese enable AI-assisted contribution workflows within Claude Code editor.\n\n---\n\n### **11. Key Design Patterns**\n\n1. **Factory Pattern** - Agent creation via provider configuration\n2. **Strategy Pattern** - Different monitoring tasks (HealthCheckTask)\n3. **Template Method** - CLI agent base class with subclass overrides\n4. **Singleton Pattern** - TrajectoryRecorder global instance\n5. **Adapter Pattern** - Filesystem abstraction\n6. **Dataclass Validation** - `__post_init__` for configuration validation\n\n---\n\n### **12. Execution Artifacts**\n\nGenerated during operation:\n```\n<repo>/.sds/\n├── deploy.sh              # Auto-generated deployment script\n├── health_check.sh        # Auto-generated health check script\n├── code_analysis.md       # Code analysis results\n├── deployment_issues.md   # Identified deployment issues\n├── config.toml           # Persisted deployment config\n├── trajectory.json       # Full execution trace\n└── logs/\n    ├── deploy_attempt_*.log\n    └── health_check_*.log\n```\n\n---\n\n### **13. System Behavior Summary**\n\nThe SDS operator implements a **self-healing deployment loop**:\n\n1. **Autonomous Analysis** - Pre-analyze codebase for issues\n2. **Script Generation** - Auto-create deployment scripts if missing\n3. **Intelligent Deployment** - Deploy and catch failures\n4. **Self-Correction** - Use AI to analyze errors and fix scripts\n5. **Automatic Retry** - Re-deploy up to configured attempts\n6. **Continuous Monitoring** - Run periodic health checks\n7. **Intelligent Analysis** - Use AI to interpret health results\n8. **Graceful Shutdown** - Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM signals cleanly\n\nAll interactions are recorded in trajectory for debugging and analysis.\n\n---\n\n### **14. Key Components & Modules**\n\n#### **A. Core Operator (app_operator/operator.py)**\n- **Main orchestrator** for the deployment & monitoring workflow\n- Manages the 3-phase lifecycle:\n  1. **Code Analysis** - Pre-deployment codebase analysis\n  2. **Deployment** - Deploy with automatic AI-assisted error recovery\n  3. **Monitoring** - Continuous health checks with intelligent analysis\n- Handles graceful shutdown via signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM)\n- Manages trajectory recording for execution traces\n\n#### **B. AI Coding Agents (agent_cli/)**\nAbstraction layer for multiple LLM providers with a unified interface:\n\n| Agent | Provider | Use Case |\n|-------|----------|----------|\n| **CodexCodingAgent** | OpenAI Codex CLI | Code generation via OpenAI |\n| **GeminiCodingAgent** | Google Gemini CLI | Generation via Google Gemini with event streaming |\n| **ClaudeCodeCodingAgent** | Claude Code CLI | AI-native generation via Anthropic's Claude |\n| **OpencodeCodingAgent** | OpenCode CLI | Code generation via OpenCode |\n\n- All agents inherit from abstract `CodingAgent` base class\n- `CLICodingAgent` provides CLI-based execution foundation\n- Factory pattern (`factory.py`) selects agents via `sds.toml` configuration\n- Agents handle timeouts, signal interruption, and stream processing\n\n#### **C. Specialized Agents**\n\n**1. DeploymentAgent** (agents/deployer.py)\n- Auto-generates `deploy.sh` and `health_check.sh` if missing\n- Executes deployment with timeout handling\n- Implements self-healing loop: deployment → failure detection → AI fix → retry\n- Supports multiple deployment platforms (Docker, Kubernetes)\n- Tracks attempt history and logs\n\n**2. CodeAnalyzerAgent** (agents/code_analyzer.py)\n- Analyzes codebase structure before deployment\n- Generates `.sds/code_analysis.md` (findings)\n- Generates `.sds/deployment_issues.md` (identified problems)\n- Uses agent to explore repo and identify deployment challenges\n\n**3. AppMonitor** (agents/app_monitor.py)\n- Runs periodic health checks at configurable intervals\n- Executes extensible monitoring tasks via `MonitoringTask` interface\n- `HealthCheckTask` - Runs `.sds/health_check.sh` and analyzes results\n- Uses agent to interpret health check output and suggest improvements\n- Tracks health check cycle count\n\n#### **D. Configuration System (config.py)**\nDataclass-based configuration with strict validation:\n\n```python\nAgentConfig       # provider, model selection\nOperatorConfig    # interval (1-86400s), deployment_max_iters, monitoring_max_iters\nDeploymentConfig  # platform (docker/k8s), target (local/remote)\n```\n\n- Configuration hierarchy: project root → target repo → `.sds/config.toml`\n- Supports TOML format via `tomllib`/`tomli`\n- Validates on initialization with clear error messages\n- Merges configurations with deep merge for overrides\n\n#### **E. Filesystem Abstraction (filesystem.py)**\n- Interface-based design for testability\n- `RealFilesystem` - Production file operations\n- `InMemoryFilesystem` - Testing without disk I/O\n- Abstracts: exists, is_dir, mkdir, read_text, write_text, chmod\n- Enables dependency injection for better unit testing\n\n#### **F. Exception Hierarchy (exceptions.py)**\nCustom exceptions with context:\n- `SdsOperatorError` - Base exception\n- `ConfigurationError` - Config validation failures\n- `DeploymentError` - Includes exit_code, attempt number\n- `FileSystemError` - File operation failures\n- `ProcessError` - Subprocess failures with timeout flag\n- `AgentError` - Agent generation/analysis failures\n\n#### **G. Trajectory Recording (tools/trajectory.py)**\nReal-time execution trace capture:\n- Records all agent interactions, prompts, responses, tool calls\n- Four phases: EXPLORATION, SCRIPT_GENERATION, DEPLOYMENT, MONITORING\n- Thread-safe singleton pattern\n- Outputs to `.sds/trajectory.json`\n- Limits output to prevent huge files (MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=10000 chars)\n- Supports Gemini session cleanup\n\n#### **H. Health Check System (tools/healthcheck.py)**\n- Executes `.sds/health_check.sh` with timeout\n- Captures stdout/stderr/exit_code\n- Writes logs to `.sds/logs/health_check_*.log`\n- Handles timeouts gracefully with partial output capture\n- Returns structured result dict\n\n---\n\n### **4. Programming Languages & Technologies**\n\n| Language | Usage | Key Files |\n|----------|-------|-----------|\n| **Python 3.10+** | Core operator, agents, tools | app_operator/*, tools/* |\n| **Bash** | Deployment/health check scripts (auto-generated) | `.sds/deploy.sh`, `.sds/health_check.sh` |\n| **Go** | Target applications (Hotel Reservation) | apps/deathstarbench/hotelReservation/* |\n| **Java** | Target applications (Train Ticket) | apps/train-ticket/* |\n| **C++/Python** | Mixed-language microservices | apps/deathstarbench/socialNetwork/* |\n| **Jinja2** | Prompt templating | prompts/*.jinja2 |\n| **TOML** | Configuration files | sds.toml, config.toml |\n\n**Key Dependencies:**\n- `langchain-openai>=1.1.6` - LLM integration\n- `langgraph>=1.0.5` - Agentic workflows\n- `python-dotenv` - Environment variable loading\n- `loguru` - Structured logging\n- `jinja2` - Template rendering\n- `pytest` - Testing framework\n\n---\n\n### **5. CLI Commands & Entry Points**\n\n**Entry Point:** `sds_operator` (bash wrapper)\n```bash\n./sds_operator run <DIR> [--config <FILE>]      # Deploy & monitor\n./sds_operator init-exp <APP_PATH> <EXP_NAME>   # Create experiment\n```\n\n**Commands Implementation:**\n- `commands/run.py` - Orchestrates AppOperator with loaded config\n- `commands/init_exp.py` - Copies app, removes git history, initializes fresh repo\n\n**Dependencies Check:**\n- Validates Docker and kubectl are installed\n- Checks Docker daemon is running\n\n---\n\n### **6. Configuration Flow**\n\n```\nsds.toml (root) or target/.sds/config.toml\n    ↓\nAgentConfig (provider selection)\n    ↓\nCreate agent via factory\n    ↓\nAppOperator initialization\n    ↓\nLoad or override via runtime flags\n```\n\n**Configuration Priority:**\n1. Project root `sds.toml`\n2. Target repo `sds.toml`\n3. Target repo `.sds/config.toml`\n4. CLI flags override\n\n---\n\n### **7.
